names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Μπορίσος και Γλιέβος οι Μάρτυρες», with the rank word left off — the Greek page's own transcription of the Slavonic name.
The baptismal name, as the same page prints it: «δια του αγίου Βαπτίσματος μετονομάσθηκαν Ρωμανός και Δαβίδ», Romanos being the elder brother's.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 2. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Борис и Гљеб.“ Свети мученици heads both brothers and belongs to neither name alone, and мученици is a rank word `honorific.js` composes, so stripping it leaves the bare forename; the heading offers no patronymic and no epithet, and „синови великога кнеза Владимира“ is the body's first words, which this corpus keeps in the English display name and not in a name form. The form meets no other folder in any language — measured, and worth saying of a name this corpus holds six times over, because not one of those folders carries a Serbian form.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Μπορίσος και Γλιέβος οι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and the page's own heading names the two brothers as two saints, so this is one folder of the two. The corpus already keeps the younger brother as `gleb-prince-and-passion-bearer`, from days.pravoslavie.ru's 5 September, where the Russian calendar keeps him alone; it keeps no folder for Boris, and this Greek line is where he arrives. He is none of the corpus's three other Borises — Boris-Michael of Bulgaria, Boris Bogolepov and Boris son of Philosophos Ornatsky. The page calls the two «Μάρτυρες» and nothing else, so `martyr` is the only type taken from it; the corpus's Gleb is `passion-bearer` and `prince` off the Russian source, which is not the source read here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, no year, no place and no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 15.05.2026 (2. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Борис и Гљеб.“

attestations.note: **The heading enumerates both brothers — „Свети мученици Борис и Гљеб.“ — so the citation above is that heading whole**, per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4 and the coordinator's ruling, and both names are folders this corpus already keeps. **The day is a third one for these two and is not a conflict**: the Greek keeps them on 24 Ιουλίου, the Russian keeps Gleb on 5 сентября, and the Prologue keeps them on 2. мај ст. ст.; no existing row was moved. The identification is beyond doubt — sons of the great prince Vladimir who baptised the Russian people, brothers by one mother, the inheritance divided before their father's death, the eldest brother Svyatopolk of Kyiv sending men who killed them in two different places, and the incorrupt and fragrant bodies at Vyshgorod healing to this day. **The Prologue gives no year for either**, so nothing was added to `dates`. New to the corpus from this page: that **Vladimir had many wives and children by them before his own baptism**, which is the reason this entry gives for the two being „браћа од једне мајке“; that the state was divided **among all his sons**; and that the two were killed „на једном месту“ and „на другом“, in two separate places rather than one. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
